evidence: The entry opened with "Six user-facing claim sites" while the same paragraph said mutation made the gate fail "8 times, once per registered claim", so it contradicted itself. The fix reworded it to eight claims across six sites.
guidance_note: When a changelog states a count, derive it from the same artifact the later sentence measures (len(Claims)) and check that every number in the paragraph agrees before pushing.

evidence: splitRow did `strings.Trim(line, "|")` on the raw line, so a trailing space after the final pipe leaves the pipe, giving 5 cells and a false "has 5 cells, want 4" error. The agent trimmed each line before the prefix check and added an edge-whitespace test.
guidance_note: When a parser normalizes whitespace in one place (Normalize), give the row splitter that reads the same file the same whitespace tolerance and test a padded row.

narrative: Round 0 raised two real, independent defects: a self-contradicting claim count in the changelog and a row parser that broke on trailing whitespace. Both were fixed in one commit, and round 1 approved with no new findings.
guidance_observations: The changelog contradicted itself inside one paragraph; a final read-through checking that the numbers agree would have caught it before review.

evidence: The changelog said "the `lit upgrade` refresh path", but the diff wires ensureNextSkillFile into quickstart_refresh.go, and the agent confirmed `lit upgrade` only swaps the binary. The line was changed to name `lit quickstart --refresh`.
guidance_note: Before naming a command in a changelog, trace the call site the diff actually wires (here quickstart_refresh.go) instead of naming it from memory.

evidence: The shipped template does teach the retired `lit ready`, but the ticket explicitly required a byte-identical move, and the CHANGELOG says so. The correction is owned by named sibling tickets (rls7.2/7.3/7.4), and #462/#463 in this batch deliver them.
This duplicates F1 on the same CHANGELOG line (`lit upgrade` vs `lit quickstart --refresh`). Commit 18a82f5 shows the single edit that fixes both.

The append-on-markerless-file behavior is real. The agent disputed the premise that many repos already carry the memento copy, since plugin skills live in the plugin cache; the packet does not show this either way, but the claim is plausible. The agent took the reviewer's fallback and added TestEnsureNextSkillFileAdoptsMarkerlessExistingFile.

A markerless override made upsertManagedSection append on every run, so the file grew without bound, and the agent confirmed this from its branches. Rather than documenting the trap, the agent normalized the content at the load boundary (wrapManagedSection), which was the better cure.
guidance_note: When writing a new consumer of an input-shape-sensitive writer (upsertManagedSection), list every input shape an override can take (no markers, begin only, end only, extra text) before writing the first normalizer.

evidence: 18a82f5's wrapManagedSection skipped wrapping on `strings.Contains(content, beginMarker)` alone, so begin-only content still grew the file. The agent replaced it with a full enumeration that rejects every malformed shape, which is broader than the reviewer's both-markers check.
guidance_note: When fixing one malformed input shape, enumerate the whole shape table (zero/one/many of each marker, text outside) in the first fix rather than guarding only the reported case.

evidence: 32001c7 validates `trimmed := strings.TrimSpace(content)` but then `return content, nil`, so whitespace outside the markers leaks into the section. upsertManagedSection consumes only one trailing newline, so each run adds a blank line. The fix returns trimmed + newline.
guidance_note: A parse-don't-validate normalizer must return the canonical form it validated, not the raw input; check that the validated value and the returned value are the same variable.

evidence: The F5 fix had made the "exactly the way" quickstart-work.md analogy true. The F6 fix in 32001c7 then added loud rejection of mixed-marker overrides, which quickstart-work.md never does, but left the CHANGELOG sentence unchanged.
guidance_note: When a fix adds a new rejection rule, re-read every doc sentence that describes that input's contract (here the CHANGELOG override analogy) in the same commit.

evidence: The flag is a false positive: 32001c7 only touched normalizeManagedSection, while the exists-vs-create branch in writeManagedFile that drops frontmatter for an empty SKILL.md predates review. The reply-hint says pushback, but the agent accepted and keyed create-vs-adopt on meaningful content in the shared writer.
guidance_note: When reusing a writer whose create branch writes a required header, test the exists-but-empty input, since that file takes the adopt branch and skips the header.

narrative: The markerless-override fix (F5) checked only the begin marker, which forced round 1 (F6). The F6 fix validated trimmed content but returned raw content (F7) and silently falsified the changelog's override analogy (F8). Round 2 also found an independent pre-existing gap (F9, empty existing file), so round 3 would have happened anyway. Round 2 itself was caused entirely by F5's incomplete fix.
guidance_observations: Each normalizer fix closed only the reported input shape; writing the full input shape table up front would have collapsed F5-F7 into one round.
The changelog analogy was edited in three rounds as the contract shifted; a doc claim about a contract should be re-checked in every commit that changes that contract.

evidence: The reviewer showed `workflows` has no Hidden:true, so no test exercised Hidden-vs-Retired, and the agent confirmed this against the binary. The agent made liveCommandNames pure and pinned the case with synthetic specs, rather than hiding a real command, and corrected the claims.
guidance_note: Before citing a concrete example in a test label or changelog ("workflows is hidden"), check the registry row it names instead of inheriting the claim from a ticket note.

evidence: fef39c1 rewrote the mid-entry hidden-but-live sentence and renamed the table case, but kept the closing sentence's "retired, unknown, hidden-but-live, and prose shapes" table-case claim. That sentence now contradicted the corrected one; the agent called it "leftover from before the previous round's correction".
guidance_note: When retracting a claim, grep the whole entry and the test comments for every occurrence of the claim's key phrase ("hidden-but-live") and fix them all in one commit.

evidence: The flag is a false positive: 5d88f32 touched only CHANGELOG.md, and the register.go Retired comment claiming "no row can state one without the others" under [LAW:types-are-the-program] was in the original PR. Go cannot refuse a same-package struct literal, so the claim was false. The agent weakened the claim and extended the coherence test to the Run facet.
guidance_note: Only cite types-are-the-program for a guarantee the compiler actually enforces; for a constructor-plus-test convention, say so and test every facet the comment claims.

evidence: The flag is a false positive: litToken's single-word capture predates review and 5d88f32 only touched CHANGELOG.md. The `bulk import` retired-subcommand gap is real. The agent took the reviewer's first option (scope the claim to top-level commands) and filed links-workflow-mrb6.
guidance_note: When stating a gate's guarantee, check whether the retired concept also exists at other levels (subcommand families) and scope the claim to what the extractor actually reads.

narrative: The F1 fix corrected one sentence about the hidden-but-live example but left the closing sentence's matching claim, which forced round 2 (F2). Round 2 then surfaced two pre-existing overclaims in the original diff (the type-enforcement comment and the top-level-only gate scope), so round 3 was needed regardless.
guidance_observations: The changelog entry was a single very long paragraph that repeated claims; every retraction needed a sweep of all copies, and the first one missed one.
Several findings were overclaims in prose (type enforces it, gate covers all commands); scoping guarantees to what the code actually enforces at authoring time would have removed round 2's findings.

evidence: The zero-state paragraph did restate quickstart-work.md:9's fall-through clause and was deleted. The first paragraph states the epic-major disposition the ticket's done-when requires the skill itself to state, so the reviewer's wholesale-pointer cure overreached. The agent kept that paragraph and added a pointer.
guidance_note: When a skill sits next to a reference doc, check each new paragraph against the reference for restated facts before pushing, and keep only what the skill uniquely owns.

narrative: Round 0 raised one partly-correct duplication finding. The agent split it: it deleted the duplicated routing paragraph and kept the disposition statement the ticket required. Round 1 approved.

evidence: The `git checkout <ticket id>` resume step does miss `<ticket id>_slug` branches. The PR only adopts the file the released binary writes, so editing it here would recreate the drift the epic removes. The agent routed the fix to the source template via ticket links-workflow-p0dw.
guidance_note: When a branch-naming instruction allows two patterns, the resume instruction must look up both; check paired create/resume steps in a template when authoring it.

evidence: Orphans and `lit next` are nested under `### In progress work`, which is a real structural oddity. "Misrepresents" and the [LAW:decomposition] framing overstate a heading-level issue. The generated file correctly stays byte-identical, and the issue is routed to the template ticket.

"pull from those first" for orphans contradicts the new epic-major rule that moving epics is never improvised, and the agent agreed it is a genuine conflict. The defect lives in the source template that #463 edited, so the fix belongs there, not in the generated copy.
guidance_note: When adding a new ordering rule to a procedure document (#463's epic-major section), re-read every earlier step that also picks work (orphans first) for conflicts with it.

evidence: The only command given is branch-scoped `gh pr list --head ...`, so the repo-wide overlap check has no concrete command. Declining the in-PR edit to a generated file and routing to ticket item 3 was right.

narrative: This dogfood PR adopted the binary-written SKILL.md verbatim. The reviewer raised four real template-content issues. The agent correctly declined to hand-edit the generated artifact and filed every one against the source template ticket links-workflow-p0dw.
guidance_observations: The template defects reached a release because #460 moved the text byte-identically and #463 only added sections; F3's conflict was introduced by #463's new section without a re-read of the existing steps.
Reviewing a generated artifact surfaces source-template bugs; routing them to the template was the right move, and it also points at reviewing template content in the PR that edits the template.

evidence: For the kex_exchange_identification reset, the selected symptom line names no host or port, so "host and port included" was an overclaim. The fix dropped the clause.
guidance_note: Before writing a general property of an output into a changelog, check it against every test fixture of that output (traceConnectionReset here).

evidence: Every test injected a zero delay function, so remoteIORetryDelay's shift and cap had no coverage, while the sibling transientRetryDelay has its own test. 2c8f1d8 adds TestRemoteIORetryDelaySchedule, which asserts 1s/2s/4s, the cap, and the clamp.
guidance_note: When a PR's headline behavior is a schedule (1s/2s/4s), test the production function that computes it, not only the loop with an injected stub.

evidence: Nothing pinned that classifyTransientGCError leaves a RemoteUnreachableError alone, so the nested retry budgets could silently compound. 2c8f1d8 adds an identity-and-errors.Is test covering exactly that.
guidance_note: When nesting a new retry loop inside an existing one, add a test that the outer classifier does not retry the inner loop's terminal error.

evidence: The reviewer named LockWorkspaceExclusive's "close other lit commands and retry" wrapper, which does not end in "retry after it completes". The comment was reworded to "Each contention wrapper carries its own retry guidance".
guidance_note: Before quoting one message's phrasing as the reason for a whole category, grep every producer of that error for its actual wording.

evidence: 2c8f1d8 rewrote the error_output.go comment for F4 and edited this same CHANGELOG paragraph for F1, yet left "its message already ends in 'retry after it completes'" in the changelog. The agent acknowledged the fix "was not carried into the changelog entry".
guidance_note: When correcting an overclaimed phrase, grep the diff for every copy of it (code comments and CHANGELOG) and fix them all in the same commit.

evidence: The flag is a false positive: runRemoteIO inside pushWithinLock and SyncFetch was in the original diff, and 2c8f1d8 only added tests and comment text. Up to 7s of sleeps under the commit lock is real, but "fail-fast in milliseconds" overstates the baseline, since a successful push already holds the lock across network I/O. The agent took the reviewer's own document-and-bound alternative.
guidance_note: When adding sleeps inside a function that runs under a lock, state the added lock-hold bound in the budget comment at authoring time.

narrative: Round 0 raised four valid findings: one overclaim, two missing tests, and one comment overclaim, all fixed in 2c8f1d8. That fix corrected the workspace-busy overclaim in the code comment but not its copy in the changelog (F5). Round 1 also raised a lock-hold concern (F6) on pre-existing code, so round 2 would have run regardless.
guidance_observations: The changelog entry duplicated reasoning from code comments, so each comment correction needed a matching changelog edit, and one was missed.
